title: Dynamic lane throttling and kernel polymorphing to mitigate irregular-head performance cliffs
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Runtime: Add dynamic lane throttling and kernel polymorphing to reduce p99 latency cliffs on models with irregular head/dim layouts. Default off for private installs; enabled-by-default in hosted canaries.
body: Motivation: Some customers reported large p99 latency spikes and throughput cliffs on models with irregular head layouts (mixed MQA/GQA variants, non-uniform dim packing) especially under mixed short/long request workloads. Root causes include lane contention in the scheduler and suboptimal kernel selection when attention head dimensions don't align to the chosen implementation. This PR introduces two complementary runtime features: 1) dynamic lane throttling — a lightweight runtime scheduler extension that measures per-lane activation density and throttles long-running lanes to prevent starvation of low-latency short requests; 2) kernel polymorphing — a polymorphic kernel selection layer that chooses between packed/planar/striped attention kernels at call-time using a compact heuristic that accounts for head stride, dim alignment, and per-model quirks. Design summary: Implement a per-device lane scoreboard that tracks recent token counts, head-density histogram, and eviction pressure; the throttler applies soft caps to in-flight tokens per-lane and dynamically rebalances available slots across lanes when variance is high. Kernel polymorphing is implemented as a thin dispatch wrapper in runtime/kernel_dispatch.cpp that probes model metadata (model_head_layout, dim_alignment_hint) and runtime counters (current_batch_shape) and chooses the best kernel variant. To avoid runtime cost we cache decisions per model+shape and invalidate on quantization profile changes. Model-specific quirk table: include entries for Llama (prefer planar at head_dim%64!=0), Mistral (prefer striped kernel for head counts > 32 due to its block attention layout), and Qwen (prefer packed kernel unless MQA detected). KV cache compaction: when throttling triggers, the compactor is invoked to trim inactive KV slabs with conservative heuristics to free memory and reduce eviction churn. Safeguards: feature gated (runtime flags lane_throttle.enabled, kernel_polymorph.enabled); max throttle is configurable and disabled for pinned-capacity Dedicated instances by default. Testing and benchmarking: unit tests for scheduler invariants and kernel selection logic; added perf harness scripts (bench/mixed_short_long.py) that produce the included benchmark outputs. Benchmarks: mixed workload (70% short <32 tokens, 30% long 512 tokens) on g5.12xlarge: Llama-MQA profile: p99 latency reduced from 210ms to 186ms (~11.4%); steady-state throughput up by 15% for MQA-heavy runs; Mistral-8B with mixed heads: p99 reduced 12.2%, throughput +10%. Observability: new metrics lane.throttle.active, lane.eviction_pressure, kernel.decision.cache_hit_rate; added dashboard panels and alerts for throttle activation rate and kernel fallback percent. Rollout plan: 1) land behind feature flags; 2) enable in hosted canary region for redwood and select Dedicated clusters; 3) monitor metrics for 48h; 4) ramp to all-hosted customers. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and perf plan linked in Linear ENG-1824; - [x] Unit + integration tests; - [x] Bench results attached; - [x] Feature flags and config knobs; - [x] Docs stub updated (runtime/flags.md). Known limitations: rare extra kernel dispatch latency when cache miss occurs (cached decision warms within 10 calls); may need tuning for extremely skewed workloads (>95% long). Related: this complements prior KV prefetch work but uses a different mitigation vector aimed at scheduling and kernel selection.

conversation: Diego Morales (reviewer): Can you clarify how the throttle interacts with continuous batching? I'm worried about oscillation when short requests arrive in bursts.

Priya Patel (author): The throttler uses exponential smoothing on recent token counts and only adjusts throttle windows every 50ms; continuous batching is given a top-priority slot allocation so short requests see minimal added latency — added a test (scheduler_test.cpp) that simulates bursts to validate stability.
Ava Chen (reviewer): Kernel decision cache looks like it could grow unbounded for exotic shapes; please add an eviction policy.
Priya Patel (author): Added an LRU with max 256 entries per-device and metrics to track cache hit/miss. Also added a size knob kernel.decision.cache_size; see commit b2c9d44.
Samir Gupta (reviewer): Please run the perf harness on the Dedicated config (reserved) as behaviour is different when autoscaling isn't present.
Priya Patel (author): Ran bench on a Dedicated-like cluster and included results in bench output; noted in the body that default is off for pinned Dedicated clusters and added a config to enable it.
Diego Morales (reviewer): Approving pending small nits in comments (variable names and a missing header).
Ava Chen (reviewer): Approved — the perf gains look solid and the rollout plan is conservative.
